text.p: Bonds fell but less than Spain as southern European markets retreated on fears that the European Union was preparing to delay the launch of its single currency.

The futures contract slid to within four basis points of key support at 107.75, chart analysts said, while the 10-year cash spread with the Bund widened to 124 basis points from 117 at Thursday's close, despite German denials of a delay.

"The market is very nervous and the selling pressure may not be over yet. Anxiety over a possible delay in the single currency hit the peripheries and put the Latins (currencies) under pressure and we could not be imune," said one trader.
For one technical analyst, if the future broke below 107.75 there was no good support before 106.50.
"If 107.75 were broken, the market could start to sell heavily and drag the (10-year) spread with the Bund towards 125 basis points," said one fixed income trader.

Traders said that the extent of any correction could be amplified by the lack of end users in the market. "The banks are just seeking to trade and could follow any greater correction that sets in abroad," said one dealer.
"We are going to have to follow (the Spanish market) as our (negative) spreads against Bonos are already too wide," said another trader.

Traders said that despite the fact that the escudo was not coming under as much pressure as the Spanish peseta or the Italian lira, there was no escaping the consequences of any delay in the single currency.
"Any delay removes the pressure on the central banks of southern Europe, notably Portugal, to be aggressive in cutting interest rates," said a trader.
